selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What new stage of faith was the traveller hoping to reach after leaving the classroom?
questions.answer: He wanted his faith to grow from knowing with certainty to a more direct, seeing-based certainty.

questions.question: Who invited the traveller at this stage, and what were they doing?
questions.answer: He was called by many spiritual guides who were seeking the truth and reaching a higher level of certainty through the way of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

questions.question: How is the place where these guides gathered described?
questions.answer: It is presented as a very wide and radiant spiritual gathering place made up of many smaller lodges and centers of remembrance and training.

questions.question: On what basis were those spiritual guides declaring Allah’s existence and oneness?
questions.answer: They were speaking from spiritual witnessing, inner disclosure, and the extraordinary signs Allah allowed to appear through them.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the strength of a truth accepted by all of those saints?
questions.answer: It shows that such a truth must be very clear and powerful, since so many spiritually refined people agreed on it.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the comparison between sunlight and many colors?
questions.answer: It helps explain that one divine source can appear through many different spiritual paths and forms while still remaining one reality.

questions.question: According to the passage, what three groups together form a very powerful united testimony?
questions.answer: The prophets, the purified scholars, and the saints together form that united witness.

questions.question: Why is their combined agreement described as brighter than daylight?
questions.answer: Because their shared testimony is presented as so strong and obvious that it points to Allah’s existence even more clearly than daylight points to the sun.

questions.question: What benefit did the traveller gain from the Sufi hospice?
questions.answer: He gained stronger faith through the united testimony of the saints about Allah’s necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that the shared witness of the saints, alongside the prophets and scholars, gives powerful support for belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why did the traveller leave the classroom and go on to another place?
questions.answer: He wanted to witness how faith becomes stronger and develops into a deeper kind of certainty.

questions.question: What kind of people did he meet in the hospice?
questions.answer: He met saintly spiritual guides known for inner insight and extraordinary spiritual gifts.

questions.question: What role does the way of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, play in their journey?
questions.answer: It is the path under which they strive for truth and reach higher spiritual certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about Sufi centers by describing many small ones joined into one vast place?
questions.answer: It suggests that many separate spiritual efforts are united in one shared purpose and light.

questions.question: What were the saints all saying together?
questions.answer: They were all affirming that only Allah is truly divine and that He necessarily exists as One.

questions.question: How did their experiences support what they were saying?
questions.answer: Their inner spiritual disclosures and the wonders connected to them served as signs confirming their testimony.

questions.question: Why are the saints called luminous and sacred geniuses in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they are portrayed as spiritually gifted people whose lives and insights reflect divine light.

questions.question: What does the image of many different colors coming from one sun teach about the saints?
questions.answer: It teaches that their different paths and spiritual states all come from one divine source.

questions.question: How does this passage connect the saints with the prophets and the purified scholars?
questions.answer: It shows that all three groups agree on the same truth about Allah, creating one broad and powerful consensus.

questions.question: What conclusion would a careful reader draw about religious diversity among true spiritual guides in this passage?
questions.answer: Their differences in style and experience do not cancel the truth; instead, they show many reflections of the same reality.

questions.question: What does the traveller desire most strongly at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He deeply wants his faith to keep growing stronger and to advance to a more direct level of certainty.

questions.question: How large is the group that summons him, and what does that detail emphasize?
questions.answer: The group is described as thousands or even millions, emphasizing the breadth and weight of their testimony.

questions.question: In what kinds of places are these spiritual guides gathered?
questions.answer: They are gathered in places of spiritual retreat, remembrance, and guidance.

questions.question: What shared message do all of these guides proclaim?
questions.answer: They all testify to Allah’s necessary existence and absolute oneness.
